rows.text: The current text of Legislative Decree 81/2008, art. 71, c. 11 gives INAIL 45 days from the employer's request for the first periodic verification. The 60-day term in Ministerial Decree 11 April 2011, art. 2, c. 1 is superseded by the statute, which ranks higher, so 45 days is the valid limit today.

rows.text: Under Article 71(2) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 (DLGS71.md, art. 71, c. 2), when choosing work equipment the employer must consider four elements: the specific conditions and characteristics of the work to be done, the risks present in the work environment, the risks arising from the use of the equipment itself, and the risks arising from interference with other equipment already in use.

Yes. Under D.Lgs. 81/2008 art. 72, comma 2 (DLGS72.md), a lessor of work equipment without an operator must certify its good condition, maintenance and efficiency at handover, and must also obtain and keep on file, for the whole rental or loan period, a self-certification from the renter (or the employer) attesting to the specific training and instruction of the users.

rows.value: il datore di lavoro (the employer) provvede affinché i controlli siano effettuati da persona competente
rows.text: Under Article 71(8)(c) of Legislative Decree 81/2008, the checks (initial, periodic and extraordinary) mentioned in letters a) and b) must be carried out by a competent person (persona competente); the employer ensures this. The employer arranges for the checks, but the checks themselves must be performed by a competent person.

Under Annex VII to Legislative Decree 81/2008, mast climbing work platforms (piattaforme di lavoro autosollevanti su colonne) require a biennial periodic verification, i.e. every two years. This is stated in row 10 of the Annex VII table.

Under Allegato III, punto 4.1 of the Decreto Ministeriale 11 aprile 2011 (DM2011), registration in the list of authorised bodies is valid for five years and can then be renewed on a specific application, after a positive review of the renewal documents.

rows.text: Under Allegato II, point 3.1.2(a) of DM 11 April 2011, the verifier of SC and SP equipment at the first periodic verification must take sight of five documents: the EC declaration of conformity, the declaration of correct installation (where legally required), load charts/diagrams (where provided), the working-area diagram (where provided), and the operating instructions. The same point also requires checking the 'registro di controllo' where it applies.

No. Under Allegato I, point 4 of the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011 (DM2011), a body that has carried out product certification may not perform the first periodic verification of the specific work equipment for which it issued the CE marking certification.

Under the Global Service specification in Appendix A of the University of Catania guideline (Art. 16.2, cappe chimiche), chemical fume hoods require semi-annual maintenance, i.e. every six months, with filter replacement handled separately on an annual basis.

Yes. The INAIL guide says that when the manufacturer requests recognition and the prototype is examined at its premises, the recognition of suitability extends to the whole series; the manufacturer then issues each user a certificate of conformity for the individual unit. This is stated in section 7 (p. 43) and section 7.1 (p. 44) of the inail-guide document.

rows.value: The RDRL (the person responsible for the laboratory's teaching or research activity) of the laboratory where the equipment is located decides, unless the Employer (Datore di Lavoro) of the structure gives a different instruction.
rows.text: Section 7.3 (Modello C - Registro d'uso della strumentazione, p. 10) of the UNIVPM Linee guida per la gestione e manutenzione delle attrezzature di laboratorio (v1.0, March 2024) says the RDRL of the laboratory where the instrument sits decides whether to set up the usage register, unless the structure's Employer directs otherwise.

Under Article 10(7) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (Machinery Regulation), when instructions are digital, the manufacturer must, at the user's request at the time of purchase, provide the instructions for use in paper format free of charge within one month. The corrigendum (CORR.md) does not change this.

Under Article 13(8) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (Machinery Regulation), the importer must keep a copy of the EU declaration of conformity at the disposal of the market surveillance authorities for at least 10 years after the machinery or related product has been placed on the market.

No. Under Article 15(3) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (Machinery Regulation, REG.md), a distributor that has reason to believe the machinery is not in conformity must not make it available on the market until it has been brought into conformity; informing the manufacturer or importer and the market surveillance authorities is required only in addition, and only where the machinery presents a risk. The Regulation applies from 14 January 2027 (Article 54), so it governs a sale on 1 March 2027.

rows.text: From 14 January 2027 Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 applies, so on 1 March 2027 it governs the lift. Vehicle servicing lifts are listed in Annex I, Part A, point 3, so Article 25(2) of that Regulation gives the manufacturer three options: (a) module B followed by module C, (b) module H, or (c) module G.

Under Article 54 of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), the Regulation applies from 14 January 2027, but the Corrigendum (CORR.md, point 10) corrects that date to 20 January 2027, so the general application date is 20 January 2027.

Under Article 50(2) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, Member States must notify the Commission of the penalty rules and implementing measures by 14 October 2026, but the corrigendum to the OJ L 169 (4.7.2023) text changes that to 20 October 2026 (CORR.md, point 4).

No. Under Article 52(1) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230, as corrected by the corrigendum (CORR.md, point 6), only machinery placed on the market in conformity with Directive 2006/42/EC before 20 January 2027 keeps that transitional protection. A machine first placed on the market on 20 January 2027 is not covered, because Article 51(2) (corrected by CORR.md, point 5) repeals the Directive with effect from that same date.

Yes. Under Article 10(8) of Regulation (EU) 2023/1230 (REG.md), which applies from 14 January 2027 under Article 54, the manufacturer may either accompany the machine with the EU declaration of conformity or, alternatively, give the internet address or machine-readable code where it can be accessed in the instructions for use and the Annex III information. A machine placed on the market on 1 March 2027 falls under this regulation.

The files do not state the penalty. Article 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 (DLGS71.md, 'art. 71, c. 11') requires the employer to subject Annex VII equipment to periodic verifications, but the sanction provision that would set the fine is not among the documents, and no file contains the penalty amount for this failure.

The files do not state the required course duration in hours. Art. 73(5) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 (DLGS73.md) leaves the duration to a future agreement of the State-Regions Conference, and no document in the folder contains that agreement or any hour figure for telescopic-handler operators. DM2011.md (Allegato VII periodic inspections) and the INAIL guide (pp. 26-28) cover only the periodic verification of telescopic handlers, not operator training.

The files do not contain the text of Annex V to Legislative Decree 81/2008, so they do not state the emergency stop requirements for work equipment built without product directives. Article 70(2) of the decree (in DLGS70.md) only says such equipment must meet the general safety requirements of Annex V. The INAIL/EBER robot-cell sheet (robot-cell-sheet.md, p. 4) cites 'D.Lgs. 81/08 All. V' and describes emergency stop rules, but those rules come from the sheet's own text, not from Annex V.

The files do not name a harmonised standard with presumption of conformity for vehicle servicing lifts under Regulation (EU) 2023/1230. Article 20(1) of REG.md (Regulation 2023/1230) only refers generally to harmonised standards whose references are published in the Official Journal. The only EN number tied to a lift in the files is DIN EN 1493, which the MA STAR two-post lift manual says the lift was tested to, and that is not a presumption-of-conformity reference. CORR.md confirms the application date moves to 20 January 2027 (Article 54).

The files do not name the Italian national market surveillance authority for machinery. Article 70(4) of Legislative Decree 81/2008 (DLGS70.md, section 'art. 70, c. 4') only refers to the 'autorità nazionale di sorveglianza del mercato competente per tipo di prodotto' without naming it, and no other document in the folder identifies it.

Position 19 (JCB 3CX-4TPC, 5000 kg, built 2010, Masua mining area) is a mobile lifting appliance over 200 kg used in the extractive sector, so under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08 (row 12) it must be verified annually, regardless of its age. The IGEA plant record lists it as an autogru in the "Area mineraria" at Masua.

Under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/2008 (DLGSALLVII.md, Allegato VII riga 13), a mobile lifting appliance above 200 kg in regular use, not older than 10 years, needs verification every two years, so on 31 December 2027 the Effer 790 (position 7, Tabella A1 of igea-equipment.md, manufactured 2017) would be on a two-year cycle. This relies on reading 'antecedente 10 anni' as 'older than 10 years'. At 31 December 2027 the crane is exactly 10 years from its 2017 build year, so if the reading is 'more than 10 years' it is not yet antecedente; the record gives only the year, so this is a judgement call.

Position 13 is the IGEA-PRIM 5t fixed overhead crane (gru a ponte scorrevole) at Pozzo Vittorio, Monteponi, Iglesias, in a mining area, built in 2017. Under Allegato VII, D.Lgs. 81/2008, a fixed lifting appliance used in extractive settings and more than 10 years old needs annual checks, so the move from biennial to annual falls when it reaches 10 years of age. The file gives only "gen-17" (January 2017), so the first day is an inference: 1 January 2027, not a day stated in the documents.

No. Crane 23 (gru a cavalletto, Lula, built 1989) falls under the annual check, while crane 13 (IGEA-PRIM 5t overhead travelling crane, built 2017) falls under the biennial check. The files do not expressly classify crane 13 as fixed; I treated it as fixed because it is an overhead travelling crane, and that classification drives the result (if it were mobile, the extractive-sector rule would make it annual). Sources: igea-equipment.md (pp. 3, 6, 8-9) and DLGSALLVII.md (Allegato VII, righe 15-16).

rows.text: Under Allegato VII of D.Lgs. 81/08, fixed lifting appliances over 200 kg used in the extractive sector and built more than 10 years ago need an annual check; as of 2026 that covers overhead travelling cranes positions 8–12 and the gantry crane at position 23 in the IGEA plant list. Position 13 (overhead travelling crane, built 2017) is not older than 10 years, so its check is biennial, not yearly.

In Table A4 (Allegato A, autogru), positions 17, 18 and 21 have a capacity above 5000 kg: 18760 kg, 7500 kg and 7500 kg. Positions 19 and 20 are rated exactly 5000 kg, so they are not greater than 5000 kg. Position 22's capacity is listed as 2095 kg. The source is the IGEA scheda tecnica, Allegato A, Tabella A4, page 7.

In Table A1 (Allegato A, p. 6 of igea-equipment.md), positions 5 and 6 are the only truck-mounted cranes with a capacity below 1000 kg (995 kg each) and a construction year before 2005 (2003 and 2004). Positions 1, 2, 3, 4 and 7 fail one or both conditions.

Under Allegato II, point 5.2.1 of the Ministerial Decree of 11 April 2011 (DM2011.md), the employer must request the ASL to carry out periodic verifications after the first at least 30 days before the deadline. Art. 2, c. 1 also gives the ASL a 30-day term for these verifications.

Yes. Allegato II, punto 5.3.3 of the DM 11 April 2011 requires the employer to notify the INAIL office territorially competent of the 'spostamento delle attrezzature' (moving of equipment), for entry in the database. IGEA's equipment schedule (Allegato B, table B1) places the GUTTER overhead travelling crane at position 10 at Masua, so moving it to another site falls under that obligation.

rows.value: Il datore di lavoro (per la lista IGEA, IGEA S.p.A.) sostiene le spese delle verifiche periodiche.
rows.text: Under Art. 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008, periodic verifications are carried out at a fee and their cost is charged to the employer (datore di lavoro). The IGEA technical sheet confirms that IGEA S.p.A. is the employer and that the fee for each lifting device is paid under its contract (point 2.7, p. 4).

rows.text: Under point 4.2.2 of the IGEA technical sheet (Scheda tecnica, p. 4-5), IGEA must give the verifier the libretto delle verifiche, the previous periodic-verification reports and the registro di controllo. Because device 8 (DEMAG, 1985) is over 20 years old and is not CE-marked, the structural verification certificate for remaining service life also applies, while the CE declaration of conformity and the installation, use and maintenance manual do not, since they apply only to CE-marked devices.

The MA STAR manual (mastar-manual.md, section 7.2.2 'Lubricating the Spindle and the Load Nut', page 31) says to check the lubrication felt for wear and/or contamination and replace it at least every 12 months, so the maximum interval is 12 months.

According to the MA STAR operating instructions (BA364501-en), section 4.4.4 'Lowering Process', the operator is responsible for ensuring that nobody is within the danger zone before lowering the vehicle, and must first remove tools, support blocks or similar obstacles from under the vehicle.

The nanoScan3 manual (section 5.6.2, "Planning the regular thorough check") says the regular tests must be carried out at least once a year. Section 5.6.2 also recommends some checks daily, but the minimum interval for the regular thorough check is one year.

Section 2.3 "Improper use" (page 11) of the SICK nanoScan3 I/O manual lists these impermissible uses, apart from the impermissible ambient conditions (outdoors, underwater, explosion-hazardous areas): use as a physical guard, access control or authorization, and detection of transparent items.

No. The UR5e User Manual, section 18 (Maintenance and Repair), under 'Robot Arm Inspection' (p. 207, UR5e 210 User Manual), has a NOTICE stating that using compressed air to clean the robot arm can damage its components, and says never to use compressed air to clean the robot arm.
The UR5e User Manual, section 17.4 Long Term Storage (page 202 of the manual), says a robot is considered long-term stored when it is stored for a period of 6 months or more.
No. The UR10e manual, section 15.1 Emergency Stop (page 199), says an emergency stop must be reset manually at the push-button that started it, not from anywhere else.

The UR10e manual, section 19 "Disposal and Environment" (p. 224 of the manual), states that the disposal of Universal Robots robots must follow the applicable national laws, regulations and standards, and that this responsibility rests with the owner of the robot.

The files identify the DEFRIES-TITANO bridge crane at position 11 (built 1978, 3000 kg, INAIL CA 194/85, matricola 11222) in IGEA's technical sheet, Allegato A table A2 and Allegato B. Section 4.2.2, point 5 of that sheet (p. 4–5) requires a structural verification certificate of residual life cycles for machines over 20 years old, but no document states how many residual life cycles that certification yields for this crane.

The files do not state a penalty for failing to submit a lifting device to the periodic verification under Article 71(11) of Legislative Decree 81/2008. DLGS71.md (art. 71, c. 11) sets the verification duty and its costs, but it contains no sanction, and no other file I searched (including DLGSALLVII.md and DLGS70.md) contains one.

The files do not give a tightening torque for the MA STAR 3.5 lift's HAS U M16 anchor rods. The MAHA operating instructions (mastar-manual.md, BA364501-en) name the anchor rod (HAS U 5.8 M16) and the adhesive mortar (HILTI HIT HY 200-A) in the technical data on p. 9, but contain no anchoring or installation torque. The only torque in that manual is 120 Nm for the wheel-engaging support screws on the MA STAR 5.5/6.5 (section 4.8, p. 22), which does not apply to the anchor rods.

The nanoScan3 operating instructions (nanoscan3-manual.md, chapter 14 Technical Data, p. 130) give PL d, PFH 8 × 10⁻⁸ h⁻¹ and mission time TM 20 years under ISO 13849, but no MTTFd value. A search of all documents in the folder for MTTF or mean time to dangerous failure found no match.

The UR5e User Manual gives the robot arm weight (20.7 kg / 45.7 lb) and the Control Box dimensions (460 × 449 × 254 mm) in the Technical Specifications on p. 18 (manual page 18 of UR5e), but it does not state the Control Box's weight. No other document in the folder gives it.
